body.statement:
Suppose that, for every \(c\in\mathcal C\), the support \(\mathcal X_c\) of \(X_{ci}\) and the set \(\mathcal T_c\) of event times not exceeding the largest required horizon are fixed and finite.  Suppose there are fixed constants \(\pi_0,\varepsilon_0,\rho>0\) such that
\[
 P_c(X_{ci}=x,U_{ci}\ge s)\ge\pi_0,
 \qquad
 h_c(s\mid x):=P_c(T_{ci}=s\mid T_{ci}\ge s,X_{ci}=x)\le1-\varepsilon_0
\]
for all \(c\), \(x\in\mathcal X_c\), and \(s\in\mathcal T_c\) on the required horizon, and such that every training complement \(\mathcal I_{cf}^-:=\{1,\ldots,K\}\setminus\mathcal V_{cf}\) has size at least \(\rho K\).  Define
\[
 \widetilde h_{cf}(s\mid x)=
 \frac{\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{cf}^-}
       \mathbf 1\{X_{ci}=x,U_{ci}=s,\Delta_{ci}=1\}}
      {\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{cf}^-}
       \mathbf 1\{X_{ci}=x,U_{ci}\ge s\}},
\]
with value zero when its denominator is zero, let
\[
 \widehat h_{cf}(s\mid x)
 =\min\{1-\varepsilon_0/2,\max(0,\widetilde h_{cf}(s\mid x))\},
 \qquad
 \widehat Q_{c,-f}(u\mid x)
 =\prod_{s\in\mathcal T_c:s\le u}\{1-\widehat h_{cf}(s\mid x)\},
\]
and set \(\widehat Q_{c,-f}(0\mid x)=1\).  Then, uniformly over the fixed cells, folds, strata, event times, and required grid coordinates,
\[
 \left|\widehat h_{cf}(s\mid x)-h_c(s\mid x)\right|=O_P(K^{-1/2}),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{TV}_{[0,t_{c\ell}]}
 \log\!\left\{\frac{Q_c(\mathord\cdot\mid x)}
                       {\widehat Q_{c,-f}(\mathord\cdot\mid x)}\right\}
 =O_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]
Consequently \(R_{cf}(\mathord\cdot\mid x)\) is of bounded variation,
\[
 \max_{c,f,\ell}\|V_{cf\ell}(X_{ci})\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(K^{-1/2}),
\]
and
\[
 \max_{c,f,\ell}
 \left\|
  \sup_{0\le u\le t_{c\ell}}
  \left|
   \frac{\widehat Q_{c,-f}(t_{c\ell}\mid X_{ci})}
        {\widehat Q_{c,-f}(u\mid X_{ci})}
   -\frac{Q_c(t_{c\ell}\mid X_{ci})}{Q_c(u\mid X_{ci})}
  \right|
 \right\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]
Thus this finite-stratum learner satisfies the event-side restrictions with \(a_K=K^{-1/2}\), and every censor learner with \(b_K=o(1)\) satisfies \(a_Kb_K=o(K^{-1/2})\).  This is an attainability certificate for the stated finite-stratum submodel only, not for generic learners or for the TCL application without verification of these conditions.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(c\), \(f\), \(x\in\mathcal X_c\), and \(s\in\mathcal T_c\), and write \(n=|\mathcal I_{cf}^-|\).  The training indices are fixed independently of the observations by the cross-fitting construction, so Assumption~\ref{ass:cell-iid} makes the \(n\) training observations independent with law \(P_c\).  Put
\[
 A_i=\mathbf 1\{X_{ci}=x,U_{ci}=s,\Delta_{ci}=1\},
 \qquad
 D_i=\mathbf 1\{X_{ci}=x,U_{ci}\ge s\}.
\]
The event-wins-ties definition of \(\Delta_{ci}\) gives
\[
 \{U_{ci}=s,\Delta_{ci}=1\}=\{T_{ci}=s,C_{ci}\ge s\},
 \qquad
 \{U_{ci}\ge s\}=\{T_{ci}\ge s,C_{ci}\ge s\}.
\]
By Assumption~\ref{ass:conditional-censoring}, conditional on \(X_{ci}=x\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 p_1&:=E_{P_c}A_i
 =P_c(X_{ci}=x)P_c(T_{ci}=s\mid X_{ci}=x)G_c(s\mid x),\\
 p_0&:=E_{P_c}D_i
 =P_c(X_{ci}=x)P_c(T_{ci}\ge s\mid X_{ci}=x)G_c(s\mid x).
\end{aligned}
\]
The assumed at-risk bound gives \(p_0\ge\pi_0\), and division is therefore valid.  Cancelling the common censor-survival factor yields
\[
 \frac{p_1}{p_0}=P_c(T_{ci}=s\mid T_{ci}\ge s,X_{ci}=x)=h_c(s\mid x).
\]

Let \(\overline A=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{cf}^-}A_i\) and \(\overline D=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{cf}^-}D_i\).  Since both summands lie in \([0,1]\), Chebyshev's inequality gives
\[
 \overline A-p_1=O_P(n^{-1/2}),
 \qquad
 \overline D-p_0=O_P(n^{-1/2}).
\]
There are only finitely many cells, folds, strata, and event times by Assumption~\ref{ass:fixed-panel} and the finite-support premise, so a union bound makes both rates uniform.  Because \(n\ge\rho K\), they are \(O_P(K^{-1/2})\).  On the event \(|\overline D-p_0|\le\pi_0/2\), whose probability tends to one uniformly, \(\overline D\ge\pi_0/2\) and
\[
 \left|\frac{\overline A}{\overline D}-\frac{p_1}{p_0}\right|
 \le \frac{2}{\pi_0}|\overline A-p_1|
     +\frac{2p_1}{\pi_0^2}|\overline D-p_0|
 =O_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]
Thus the zero-denominator convention is used only on an event with probability tending to zero.  Projection onto \([0,1-\varepsilon_0/2]\) is nonexpansive and the true hazard belongs to \([0,1-\varepsilon_0]\), so
\[
 \max_{c,f,x,s}|\widehat h_{cf}(s\mid x)-h_c(s\mid x)|=O_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]

Assumption~\ref{ass:event-origin-support} and the finite event-time support imply the conditional product representation
\[
 Q_c(u\mid x)=\prod_{s\in\mathcal T_c:s\le u}\{1-h_c(s\mid x)\}.
\]
The constructed learner has the analogous finite product and equals one at the origin.  Define
\[
 A_{cf}(u\mid x)
 =\log\!\left\{\frac{Q_c(u\mid x)}{\widehat Q_{c,-f}(u\mid x)}\right\}
 =\sum_{s\in\mathcal T_c:s\le u}
  [\log\{1-h_c(s\mid x)\}-\log\{1-\widehat h_{cf}(s\mid x)\}].
\]
The true factors are at least \(\varepsilon_0\), and clipping makes the estimated factors at least \(\varepsilon_0/2\).  The mean-value theorem therefore bounds every summand in absolute value by
\[
 \frac{2}{\varepsilon_0}
 |\widehat h_{cf}(s\mid x)-h_c(s\mid x)|.
\]
The path \(A_{cf}\) has only the fixed finite set of possible jumps \(\mathcal T_c\).  Hence
\[
 \operatorname{TV}_{[0,t_{c\ell}]}(A_{cf})
 \le\frac{2}{\varepsilon_0}
 \sum_{s\in\mathcal T_c:s\le t_{c\ell}}
 |\widehat h_{cf}(s\mid x)-h_c(s\mid x)|
 =O_P(K^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly over all displayed indices.  This proves the log-total-variation assertion and also \(\sup_u|A_{cf}(u\mid x)|=O_P(K^{-1/2})\).

Because \(R_{cf}=\exp(A_{cf})-1\), composition of a bounded-variation path with the exponential map gives
\[
 V_{cf\ell}(x)
 \le \exp\{\sup_{0\le u\le t_{c\ell}}|A_{cf}(u\mid x)|\}
      \operatorname{TV}_{[0,t_{c\ell}]}(A_{cf})
 =O_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]
The paths have finitely many jumps and strictly positive product factors, so bounded variation holds for every training sample, not merely asymptotically.  Since every \(\mathcal X_c\) is fixed and finite,
\[
 \|V_{cf\ell}(X_{ci})\|_{L_2(P_c)}
 \le\max_{x\in\mathcal X_c}V_{cf\ell}(x)
 =O_P(K^{-1/2}),
\]
uniformly over the fixed indices.

Finally, for \(0\le u\le t=t_{c\ell}\),
\[
 \log\!\left[
  \frac{\widehat Q_{c,-f}(t\mid x)/\widehat Q_{c,-f}(u\mid x)}
       {Q_c(t\mid x)/Q_c(u\mid x)}
 \right]
 =-\{A_{cf}(t\mid x)-A_{cf}(u\mid x)\}.
\]
The absolute value of the right-hand side is bounded by \(\operatorname{TV}_{[0,t]}(A_{cf})\).  All four survival ratios lie in \([0,1]\), and the elementary bound \(|e^z-1|\le e^{|z|}|z|\) consequently yields the stated uniform \(O_P(K^{-1/2})\) ratio error.  Passing to \(L_2(P_c)\) again uses only the fixed finite covariate supports.  Taking \(a_K=K^{-1/2}\) proves both event-side rates, and if \(b_K=o(1)\), then
\[
 a_Kb_K=K^{-1/2}b_K=o(K^{-1/2}).
\]
This completes the finite-stratum certificate.
body.justification: The certificate demonstrates that the disclosed path-variation condition is attainable by an explicit data-driven learner on a transparent finite-stratum submodel.
body.gap: It proves root-\(K\) hazard, log-total-variation, relative-survival variation, and survival-ratio rates from primitive finite-support, at-risk, hazard-gap, and fold-size conditions; it does not claim generic learner coverage.
body.consumer: It can guide a discretized implementation but does not certify the support or learner conditions in the TCL application.
